# GPU stack check

Day-0 check of SPEC §9, re-run any time with
`CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1 uv run aerosurr env check --md docs/gpu_check.md`.
It confirms the GPUs are idle (via nvidia-smi, before CUDA init), that torch sees both
RTX 5090s with `sm_120` kernels, and measures bf16 GEMM throughput and a `torch.compile`
round trip per device. The block below is the verbatim command output.

GEMM: square bf16 `a @ b` (fp32 accumulate), timed with CUDA events after warm-up. Compile smoke test: `torch.compile` (inductor, default mode) of an attention + MLP block (B=4, N=2048, d=256, 8 heads), forward + backward, compared with eager; it passes when the relative L2 difference of the output is below 1e-2 (bf16 has a 2^-8 ulp). First-call time includes compilation and depends on whether the inductor/Triton caches under `~/aero/cache` are warm.

## Notes (hand-written)

- 229–231 TFLOPS dense bf16 is slightly above the ~210 TFLOPS dense FP16/BF16 figure
  usually quoted for the RTX 5090; the cards boost above the spec-sheet clock. Treat this
  as the practical ceiling for the surrogate's GEMMs.
- `torch.compile` needs a Python with headers (Triton builds a small C launcher). The
  system Python 3.12.3 has no `python3.12-dev`, so the venv uses uv-managed CPython
  3.12.15 under `~/aero/tools/python`; no sudo was needed.
- Compiler caches live in `~/aero/cache/{torchinductor,triton}` (set by
  `aerosurr.ops.configure_runtime`), and `CUDA_DEVICE_ORDER=PCI_BUS_ID` makes torch
  indices match nvidia-smi (GPU 0 = bus 01, GPU 1 = bus C2).
